scope: Lightweight extensible Python Agent Harness; coding and CLI are default applications. Natural-language plugins, frozen benchmarks and complete failed/cancelled trajectories remain; distillation and training code are removed.

capabilities.core: One model/tool loop, permission checks, context, cancellation and Journal; no workspace, coding components, Node, YAML or model SDK required on import.
capabilities.coding: Optional tasks/repository/skills/hooks/mcp/checkpoints; bounded parallel batches, cancellable finite jobs and full-access session services. Confirmed job cancellation stays local; session exit reaps owned services.
capabilities.defaults: Host full-access + never. No independent intent routing, full inventory, automatic checkpoints, mandatory completion gate or cumulative Harness budget. Model-proposed finish criteria bind only under caller-required acceptance reconciliation.
capabilities.plugins: Explicit trusted PluginHost; tools, services, providers, hooks, children and completion checks. Fixed independent acceptance and portable delivery require rechecking in the new environment.
capabilities.evaluation: Official task images and frozen conditions use public open_runtime; preparation concurrency queues outside official phase clocks. Docker query errors and bounded pre-grader patch capture remain separate from agent results. Caller deadlines, cgroup facts and service handoff preserve the independent grader; phase failures and raw rewards remain separate. Normal/strict is explicit; missing historical field retains strict.
capabilities.trajectories: Journal-only default; complete model/tool facts, bounded redacted provider/tool exception chains, cancellation origins, failed attempts and background job lifecycle. Offline ATIF/OpenAI exports preserve diagnostics, origin turns and active/transferred jobs; no training or distillation framework.
capabilities.legacy: Old RPC/SQLite and history readers remain opt-in; modern worker/runtime/benchmark code does not import the old control plane.

last_verified_baseline.scope: All six CI jobs passed for this exact commit: Windows and Ubuntu portable regression, SDK/plugin delivery, and dependency checks. Native isolation acceptance and live model experiments remain separate.

release_validation.local_checks: Offline cancellation, public benchmark assembly, actual Windows/Linux process ownership and service handoff, long-job waits, caller deadlines, cgroup limits, provider diagnostics, bounded installer recovery and failure/export regressions passed. Logging measured with synthetic streams; no Journal rewrite based on unverified model latency.
release_validation.scope: CI acceptance belongs to the exact commit/tag workflow run. Historical baseline checks do not certify new source; local checks do not imply remote CI passed.

historical_release_evidence.boundary: Historical v0.1.1 reported scores, feedback protocol, missing raw-trial evidence and the 448-test statement are maintained together in the linked record. They are not current-source acceptance.

historical_work.boundary: Previous native/live experiments retain their exact source, authorization, budget, attempts and results. No automatic rerun or transfer of old model authorization.

remaining_work: Full native OS read/network/hard-resource isolation and macOS native ownership integration remain unverified optional extensions.
Domain-specific Personal/Robot integrations and new-model/public benchmark scores need their own evidence.
npm/PyPI registry publication is separate from the source release/tag; no registry publication is implied.
verification_policy: Separate deterministic checks, native platform acceptance, packaged installation and paid model experiments. Logs stay under ignored .local/implementation or CI artifacts; never replace missing evidence with inferred success.
